model_interpretation.claim: Assigning contiguous x coordinates to each warp should improve coalescing relative to the baseline's four-x-wide tile. Having each thread produce four consecutive y outputs lets it reuse a 12-row neighborhood in registers and removes shared memory and barriers; the extra global load requests per output and register use may offset those gains, so correctness and full-run latency need controller measurement.

items.subject: Register reuse across multiple y outputs
items.objective: Implement and measure register-blocked y outputs: assign contiguous x elements across warp lanes and have each thread compute multiple nearby y outputs, reusing their overlapping input neighborhood in registers rather than shared memory. Explore a small number of outputs per thread and suitable launch geometry; preserve exact coefficients and baseline halo mapping, compute every output from current A, and use no additional allocation or launch. Compare oracle correctness and full-run latency.
